notes: CONVERGENCE: the skill's discriminating value is entirely in eval-1 (run): +0.50 (6/6 vs 3/6), same as iter-1. Baseline again correctly diagnosed the FR-G5 exit-2 gate but GAVE UP ('editing host settings.json out of scope / no bypass flag'); the skill applied the empty-HOME workaround and got a real result. That workaround is the skill's core value.

The NEW authoritativeness eval (eval-3) did NOT discriminate: 4/4 in BOTH configs. The baseline (opus) READ THE EVAL SOURCE and independently found _NullLifecycleExecutor (commands.py:1357/1386), the --json warning suppression (commands.py:1879), and the vacuous-PASS path (runner.py:419) — concluding NON-AUTHORITATIVE unaided. A capable base model rediscovers the skill's KNOWLEDGE from source; knowledge content alone does not beat a strong baseline.

Therefore the M2-authoritativeness skill edit does NOT move the benchmark against an opus baseline — but it is still worth keeping for: (a) RELIABILITY (guarantees the caveat every run rather than relying on agent thoroughness/token spend), (b) WEAKER models that won't dig through source, (c) the run-report TEMPLATE making it a required field. Honest read: the edit hardens behavior, it doesn't raise the score vs a strong model.

Token note (timing.json): baseline trust-the-pass spent 118K tokens REDISCOVERING the null-executor fact from source; with_skill spent 99K with the fact pre-stated but still ran --verbose to confirm. The skill's token advantage is real but modest here because confirmation still costs.

Bonus catch (baseline trust-the-pass): also found the --no-pty -> all-SKIPPED-but-exit-0 path (commands.py exit keys only on failed/errored/timeout) as a SECOND way a green run can be hollow — a real, independent hardening idea for the suite.
